anomalies.observed: On the Power sheet the +12V rail wire is drawn running vertically through J7 pin 1 and J7 pin 2 with junctions at both pins (and the +12V symbol also feeds J8 pin 2), so pins 1 and 2 of the fan headers are on the +12V net rather than only pin 2.
anomalies.expected: The specification lists only pin 2 of each fan header on the 12 V rail: 'the two fan-header 12 V pins (J7/J8 pin 2)'. On a standard 4-pin fan header pin 1 is the fan ground return, so it should be tied to GND, not to +12V.

evidence.quote: Also on this net: ... and the two fan-header 12 V pins (`J7`/`J8` pin 2).
Power sheet: +12V power symbol wired down through J7 pin 1 and pin 2 (junction dots) and to the J8 connector

anomalies.impact: The fan's ground-return pin is held at +12 V, so a standard fan receives no return path (effectively reverse supply) and will not spin; the firmware's fan-stall monitor would then trip RunFailureReason and abort the oven run.

anomalies.observed: An additional 2-pin screw terminal J5 is drawn with pin 2 tied to the HEATER net (the ESP32 GPIO1 / U6 IN & DIAG_EN logic net) and pin 1 to GND.
anomalies.expected: The specification describes exactly one heater output connector, J6, fed by the switched output of U6 (OUT pin 7). A connector placed directly on the 3.3 V GPIO1/HEATER control net is not described and would expose the MCU logic drive rather than the switched 12 V heater output.

evidence.quote: MCU sheet: Screw_Terminal_01x02 J5 pin 2 wired to the net labelled HEATER, pin 1 to GND

anomalies.impact: Any load attached to J5 is driven from the ESP32 GPIO1 logic net instead of the switched 12 V heater output, so it would not receive heater power and would load the GPIO.

parsed.summary: The schematic matches the specification on all explicitly stated values and connections (SPI, CS, heater switch, power mux, buck, thermocouple channels, CC resistors, ILIM/SS/boot components), but the fan-header wiring appears to put +12V on pin 1 as well as pin 2 (spec and standard fan pinout require pin 1 = GND), and an unexplained extra screw terminal J5 sits on the GPIO1 HEATER control net.
